rules.sentence: A perinephric abscess can result from complications of pyelonephritis or hematogenous spread of infection.
A perinephric abscess should be considered in a patient who does not improve despite appropriate antibiotics therapy.
CT with contrast is the best imaging modality for diagnosis of perinephric abscess and evaluation of abscess extension into surrounding organs.
Surgery is indicated in the setting of anatomic abnormality and when the abscess is too large for effective percutaneous catheter drainage and antibiotics treatment.
